correctness.rationale: The argument gives both a rigorous upper bound and a matching subgroup. Exact intersection arithmetic recovers the published counts \(n_2=108,n_3=40,n_5=16,n_8=5\) and identifies the five eightfold points. Their unique four-collinear subset forces every projective automorphism to fix \([0:0:1]\) and preserve \(z=0\). The four points on \(z=0\) have cross-ratio \(-1\), hence only eight \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\) actions are possible. Exhaustive exact lifting leaves two actions over each, and all \(16\) are checked on all \(33\) lines. The displayed generators have orders \(8\) and \(2\) and satisfy the dihedral relation.

value.rationale: The source emphasizes both the regular-octagon origin and rigidity of \(\mathcal O_{33}\), making its exact projective symmetry group a natural intrinsic invariant rather than an arbitrary computation. Determining the full stabilizer separates visible polygonal symmetry from possible accidental projective symmetries and provides explicit generators useful for orbit reductions in incidence, unexpected-curve and Lefschetz computations attached to this arrangement.
